profile.title: CMMC 2.0 Level 1 self-assessment
profile.description: Fifteen practices, assessed annually by the contractor itself, each MET or NOT MET, with an annual affirmation by a senior official. The strictest regime automat models in one specific respect: no POA&M is permitted, so a single unmet practice means there is nothing to affirm.

citations.title: Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Program
citations.note: The CMMC Program rule. Level 1 practices are enumerated at 170.14(c)(1), which is the citation catalogs/cmmc-l1.json's control ids follow.

citations.title: Contractor Compliance with the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Level Requirement
citations.note: The contract clause that makes a CMMC level a condition of award.

citations.title: Basic Safeguarding of Covered Contractor Information Systems
citations.note: The fifteen Level 1 practices derive from this clause's safeguarding requirements; it is the control-text source in catalogs/cmmc-l1.json's artifact.sources.

control_catalogs.note: Fifteen practices. The instrument names them exactly, so there is nothing for an operator to determine about scope of controls — only about scope of system.

signed_by: A senior official of the contractor (the affirming official)
assessment.notes: No third-party assessor is involved at Level 1; the contractor assesses itself and a senior official affirms the result. automat generates the packet that official reads and never the affirmation itself (docs/assessment-reporting.md invariant 1) — a generated document that looked like the affirmation would be a document someone could sign without having done the assessment.

poam.notes: No POA&M is permitted at Level 1. This is why an objective with neither machine evidence nor an operator determination must render NOT MET rather than 'in progress': there is no state in this regime between met and not, so 'in progress' would invent one — and the comfortable one. An operator reading four practices as 'in progress' concludes they are nearly there; the same four as NOT MET tells them there is nothing to affirm this year until those four are done.

submission.notes: The affirmation is entered by the affirming official. automat formats nothing for it.

applicability.trigger: A DoD contract or subcontract containing the CMMC clause at a level of 1, where the contractor processes, stores, or transmits Federal Contract Information. Whether a given award carries the clause and at what level is a contracting question — read the award, and ask your contracts office. automat does not and cannot determine this.
hints: The award or subcontract includes 48 CFR 252.204-7021
The solicitation or award states a required CMMC level of 1
The work involves Federal Contract Information but not Controlled Unclassified Information
exclusions: Acquisitions solely for commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) items

policy_caveat: automat encodes a technical reading of published policy. It is not legal advice and not a compliance determination. The agreement, award terms, or contract clause your institution signed governs; your sponsored programs office, contracts office, or counsel decides what applies and which revision. Where policy is ambiguous — for example the NIH 800-171 revision question — automat records the operator's declaration rather than resolving it. Policy citations carry effective dates and change; verify against the primary source before relying on them.

sources.title: FAR 52.204-21 Basic Safeguarding of Covered Contractor Information Systems (vendored control text)
sources.note: The control text behind the fifteen practices, already vendored for the catalog compile. A test asserts this hash still matches the file on disk, so a re-vendor that changes the text without updating this profile fails the build rather than leaving the profile citing bytes that no longer exist.

sources.title: 32 CFR 170.14(c)(1) practice-identifier crosswalk (vendored)
sources.note: The mapping from FAR clause paragraphs to CMMC Level 1 practice identifiers, which is what makes catalogs/cmmc-l1.json's control ids traceable to the rule.
